summary: Mrinal Kaul is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a PhD from Concordia University (2009–2016). He taught at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Manipal Academy of Higher Education before joining IIT Bombay as Associate Professor in 2025.

Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is an Indologist and philosopher. He served as a Professor at Vidyasagar College (attested 1970–1975) and later worked in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta, where he was attested as Lecturer in 1982.

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at Leipzig and Heidelberg, and became a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Muhamad Saputra is a PhD student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), where he studies under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

Muhamed Riyaz Chenganakkattil is an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD from IIT Delhi in 2024. That same year, he served as an Early Doc Fellow at IIT Delhi and became a Postdoctoral Fellow at Ghent University.

Muhammad Ashraf Khan works in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He has served as Deputy Director of the Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

Muhammad Nasim Khan is a scholar of archaeology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who earned an M.Phil from the University of Peshawar. He served there as Assistant Professor of Archaeology (attested 2006–2016) and held a visiting fellowship at the Royal Asiatic Society.

Muhammad Shahidullah (1885–1969) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi. He held key posts at the University of Dhaka (~1921–1954), the University of Rajshahi, and the Bangla Academy.

Muhammed Niyas Ashraf is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the Free University of Berlin (2015–2024) and was appointed a Post Doctoral Fellow at Ghent University for 2025–2026.

Mukesh Mehta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at Banaras Hindu University (2019–2022). In 2023, he worked as a Research Associate at the International School for Jain Studies.

Mukund Lalji Wadekar is an Indologist who served as Officiating Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2002–2008), Officiating Director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 2008), and General Editor of the Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 2008).
Mukund Ram Shastri (d. 1921) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Head Pandit at the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1911 and 1916–1918).

Mukunda Raj Aryal is an Indologist and historian who earned an M.Phil. from Tribhuvan University (2019–2021). He was attested as a Professor at Tribhuvan University in 2003 and served as Head at Apex College in 2017.

Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and trained under Seisetsu Seki. He served as president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), abbot of Shofuku-ji (~1949–1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies (1964).

Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his MA and PhD from the University of Queensland under Roderick S. Bucknell. He served as a Lecturer in Studies in Religion at the University of New England from 2003 to 2025.

Munenobu Sakurai (b. 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1986–1989). He served as an assistant professor at Iwate University (~1993–2005) and became a professor at Tohoku University (~2005).

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indology and computational scholar who earned a PhD from Harvard University (~1974–1979). He served as an assistant professor at the Tokyo Institute of Technology before becoming an assistant professor (~1989–1990) and professor (~1990–2009) at Kyoto University.
Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1910–1913) and was taught by Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki (~1909–1913).

Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Central Asian studies who earned a Dr.phil. from the University of Vienna under the supervision of Brigitte Marschall (attested 2010).

Munis D. Faruqui (b. 1967) is an Indologist and historian. He became an Associate Professor at the University of California, Berkeley in 2005 and served as Director and Sarah Kailath Chair of India Studies at the Numata Center (~2014).
